utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Good morning. This is Case Number IT-00-39-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Loukas, I hope that you believe me that what I'm going to say now didn't come up in my mind over the last five minutes, but already yesterday. Yesterday, we were confronted with a sometimes very repetitious questioning of the accused -- of the witness. For example, I think you asked him three, four, five times that he certainly as a lawyer would be aware that a statement should be complete. The Chamber does not consider this repetition to very much assist the Chamber. So therefore, I'm not saying this in order to regain time lost, but we had this already in our minds yesterday. We discussed it among the Judges. So would you please keep that in mind. I'd rather speak about this in the absence of the witness. That's why I asked the witness not to be in the courtroom at this very moment. But Mr. Usher, would you now escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you want to note the record of who is appearing today for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see there are some changes. And I should have mentioned that yesterday. Mr. Stewart was mentioned yesterday as being absent. Good morning, Mr. Karabeg. Mr. Hannis, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Tom Hannis for the Office of the Prosecutor. I'm assisted by Mr. Timothy Resch, and our case manager acting today is Mr. Willem Wijermars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. He already replaced yesterday in the middle of the court hearing Mrs. Annink-Javier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony the day before yesterday. The cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The cross-examination will now continue. Ms. Loukas, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, when we left off yesterday, we were dealing with the question of what was contained in your statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And just in relation to that, we got to the point where it's the fact that in your statement it's not stated -- you haven't mentioned any names in that particular paragraph, paragraph 12, that we were dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Perhaps if the witness might have the numbered paragraph statement before him.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I think you have it before you now, Mr. Karabeg. So that's the point to which we got to yesterday, where I was asking questions about the fact that you did not -- you've stated there in your statement, "He did not mention any names." And of course, you haven't in your statement mentioned anywhere the names Krajisnik or Brdjanin. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, the fact is you did not mention the names Brdjanin or Krajisnik in your Bosnian statement. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Nor in your -- nor to Ms. Brenda Hollis when she was taking your 1997 statement, the outline. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, that wasn't of interest to me at the time. What was of interest to me were the people who incarcerated me and did what they did to me. So that is why it wasn't interesting to me and I didn't mention it. Now, of course, again I would present a whole set of new facts because I learned a lot since then. I never even imagined when I made the statement that I would ever be sitting here today in court as a witness in the Krajisnik trial. And perhaps had I ever imagined that, maybe some names would have been mentioned. But all I did was to present the sequence of events in my statement, the sequence of events as they happened. So this is only a very small, minute part of what happened to me from the 25th of May 1992 to the 31st of October 1992. So it's a very tiny small excerpt from my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, we only have a limited time for cross-examination, so it would help if you actually answered the question and answered it in rather not a speech. Do you understand me, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer with a yes or with a no. But don't you hold speeches to me either and I will just give you yes or no answers, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, I don't want to get into an argument with you. I just want you to agree with me that you did not mention it in your Bosnian statement or in your 1997 statement or your 1999 statement. None of those statements. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, indeed, when you put together your corrections in May 2002, just prior to giving evidence in the Brdjanin trial, you didn't put that in your correction statement either, did you, Mr. Karabeg, this question of Brdjanin or Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And -- well, I don't want to waste time by presenting the correction statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I take it the Prosecution concedes it doesn't appear in the correction statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We agree with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that's clear for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, the other aspect, Mr. Karabeg, is that of course when you put together your correction statement just prior to giving evidence in the Brdjanin trial, you knew you were giving evidence in the Brdjanin trial, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But you didn't put the name Brdjanin and Krajisnik in that statement either. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's the fact that he knew at that stage that he was giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the statement was never corrected and the Chamber considers this witness of a level of competence that he would have known where he was testifying, in what case, and what it was about. So it's entirely clear the point you make. So if needed, one more question about it, but then it has been sufficiently dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. So we come to the Brdjanin/Talic trial, and then you have this to say at pages 6096 of the transcript. It's page 6096 of the Brdjanin -- the transcript in the trial against Mr. Brdjanin and the late General Talic. You were asked this question: "What did he say to you about the integration of Sanski Most into the Banja Luka region?" And you said: "He said that they didn't put it forward as yet, but they will, and they will place it on the agenda under pressure from Banja Luka, that is, the pressure exerted by Krajisnik and Brdjanin." Now, do you know where Mr. Krajisnik's from?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I should just like to say in response that Vrkes didn't come to me and said nothing special. It was an agreement with respect to the purchase of an apartment, and he was purchasing an apartment from a man I knew. And we sat down, it was just by chance --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... all I'm asking you is that this is what you said in the Brdjanin and Talic trial. That you placed it on the agenda under pressure from Banja Luka, that is, the pressure exerted by Krajisnik and Brdjanin. Are we agreed on what you stated in that particular trial?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that as far as the name goes is true when it comes to Krajisnik, but that I was not sure whether it was Brdjanin or Kupresanin, which of the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry. That last answer. Are you saying you're not sure whether it was Brdjanin and Krajisnik or Krajisnik and Kupresanin now?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand what you want from me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if we are referring to transcripts, the Chamber has not the relevant page in front of it at this very moment. So we can't check it. But I take it that the Prosecution has. Let's assume that whatever is in the transcript, unless it's highly improbable, that we accept that this transcript, made under the responsibility of the Registry, reflects the words of the witness at that time. So therefore, you can confront the witness with the fact that he said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. You can put questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So in any event, Mr. Karabeg, you concede that what your answer was in the former trial was, "He said he didn't put it forward as yet, but they will and they will place it on the agenda under pressure from Banja Luka, that is, under pressure exerted by Krajisnik and Brdjanin." Now you agree that that's what you said on the last occasion, when you gave evidence in the other trial. Are we agreed there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having said that. I'd like to see it, where that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, that's on the transcript from that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is what he said, according to the transcript. We agree to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, it has just been read to you what is on the transcript. The transcript is made, and it's a literal report of what you said. If you say "I don't remember," that's fine. If you say "I didn't say that," we'll then check it. If you say "I don't remember but it could be," then we take it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd like to check it. I don't know. I don't know which number the document and line is. I have it -- I have the document, but I don't know what the line was where I said that in the transcript. 27, 97, 57, what? I would like to see it myself. What are you reading from? I would like to see what you are reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Ms. Loukas is reading from -- I'll read it to you. Ms. Loukas, do you have that, because we only have a transcript of the cross-examination. Would you have a copy for me? Mr. Usher, could you...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Page 6096, as I indicated earlier, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll not look at your notes, Ms. Loukas, apart from not being able to read them. Mr. Karabeg, this is a transcript of your testimony in the -- I do not find a date at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was from Monday, the 27th of May 2002. And perhaps we should advise him as well that we do not have a transcript version of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have a transcript in English. All your words spoken in your own language are immediately translated into English and French, and this is what the English text says, your testimony on the 27th of May. Yes. Question and answer is a bit confused here. I'll read to you the questions and the answer. The question was: "Now, as far as Sanski Most integrating into the Banja Luka region, did you ever discuss this matter with any of the senior SDS members at Sanski Most?" Your answer was: "Yes, I did discuss it with the president of the municipal board of SDS of Sanski Most, with Brkic." "And what did he say to you about the integration of Sanski Most into the Banja Luka region?" "He said that they didn't put it forward as yet, but that they will, and they will place it on the agenda under pressure from Banja Luka, that is, from the pressure exerted by Krajisnik and Brdjanin." Next question was: "Now, did he specifically mention those two names to you, Krajisnik and Brdjanin, as far as you can remember, that that's where the pressure was coming from in Banja Luka?" Your answer was: "Yes, he did, because we were really exceptionally close, we had very good relations. There was empathy between the two of us. Don't misunderstand it. That person studied in Novi Sad, but he was from Sanski Most, and our first contacts were such that we then became friends." Then about the name, next question is: "Now, Mr. Karabeg, in the transcript it says that the president of the municipal board of the SDS of Sanski Most was Brkic. Can you give the Court the full name of this man that you're speaking about, this man with whom you had empathy." And then you answered: "Vlado Vrkes is the name." I read to you the testimony you gave in the -- does this sound familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please return the transcript to Ms. Loukas. Ms. Loukas will put questions to you on this issue and your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, His Honour has read to you the relevant portions from your previous testimony in the Brdjanin/Talic case. Now, when you gave evidence in this particular case on Monday, the 24th of May, you gave this evidence: "And because we were good friends and we were close" - referring to Vrkes - "I asked him how come you want to place this on the agenda now at this point for the first time?" And he said that they had received an order to that effect in Banja Luka. He said that this was done pursuant to an order issued by Krajisnik, an instruction by Krajisnik. And then I asked him whether it was pursuant to an order by Brdjanin, but he didn't know exactly who was the person who issued the specific order." Now, that's what you said on page 97 of the transcript on Monday, the 24th of May 2004, a couple of days ago. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that's what it says, let it stand. Let it remain so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Karabeg, we've all already been through the fact that it doesn't appear in any of your statements. It appears for the first time in the Brdjanin and Talic trial, and then all you're talking about in Brdjanin and Talic is pressure. When you come to give evidence in this court, you've stepped it up a notch 12 years after the event. Now it's pursuant to an order issued by Krajisnik, an instruction by Krajisnik. Now, you never said anything like that in your Brdjanin and Talic evidence, did you? You have to agree with that, Mr. Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So moving on to the next topic, yesterday we were dealing with the fact that you said you saw Talic on TV and you also saw Krajisnik there and you would not concede that you were possibly mistaken about that. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course, that's another topic on which it doesn't appear in your Bosnian statement, doesn't appear in your 1997 statement, doesn't appear in your 1999 statement, and doesn't appear in the corrections. I take it the Prosecution will concede that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We agree he does not mention Krajisnik by name as being in that televised report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. And of course yesterday, when dealing with this particular topic, you went from saying in your evidence in chief "I believe" to saying in cross-examination that you're more certain, to saying you probably saw him but refusing to concede that it was a possibility you didn't. Are we agreed on those propositions?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, but you only contributed to that with your way of examining.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, I won't get into an argument with you, Mr. Karabeg. The fact is you don't mention any of these matters in your statements, but when you come to court, you seem to add additional matters. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have indicated, it's because of the chronology of the events that one feels it is necessary to add something. So yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now -- and of course, this meeting that you've referred to in March 1991, there's nothing about that meeting in any of your statements - your Bosnian statement, the 1997 statement, the 1999 statement, your correction statement - this meeting that you say occurred in March 1991 where you received an invitation that was left on your desk. There's nothing about that in any of your statements either, is there, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is still a lot which I experienced during that period of time but I failed to mention. Like I said yesterday, I'm not a robot, I'm not a computer. It is simply impossible for me to remember everything at once. Because at the time I was giving my statement, I talked about the things that were on my mind at the time, that I felt I was able to talk about. And there was no mention of the possibility of my being a witness or giving a statement about such-and-such person.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You're saying that when the Prosecution took your statement from you, they didn't tell you that you might be possibly called as a witness in cases?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah, they merely took a statement. They never said anything about that. Because a number of people gave a statement but were never called upon to testify.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, I won't mention the fact that you're a lawyer again, Mr. Karabeg. I'm moving on to this meeting. Now, in relation to this particular meeting, when you gave evidence about that on Monday, you said that when you went to this meeting, various statements were made, including it was mentioned for the first time that Bosanska Krajina should be cleansed of the non-Serb people, that is, that the media should be stifled first, and then what have you. And then you went on to say that a judge of the misdemeanor court spoke. He said that resources should be obtained from the penalties and taxes accrued would be siphoned off to this fund which would finance the functioning of Serbian media and Serbian television, and you went on in that vein. Now, when you gave evidence in the Brdjanin/Talic trial, Mr. Karabeg - and that's at page 6071 for the Court - you didn't mention anything about ethnic cleansing and you didn't mention anything about a judge who wanted to siphon funds off and do these things. Do you concede that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I don't remember at this point that I stated that it was the president of the court from Srbac that the funds should be redirected. I think I said that he indicated that he would redirect the funds that are collected from taxes and fines, normally collected by the misdemeanors court.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, I'll read out to you what's transcribed, Mr. Karabeg. "And I remember very well when Judge Srbac" - and I corrected that later to say it was a judge from Srbac --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not Judge Srbac, the president of the misdemeanors court from Srbac. I never said that his name was Srbac.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, Ms. Loukas is now reading from the transcript. And as you certainly will remember, initially it was translated to us as "Judge Srbac" and it was then later rectified that it was the judge of Srbac. So please listen. That's not the main issue at this moment. What follows is the main issue. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So you said this: "... a judge of the misdemeanor court, said that the resources obtained from the penalties and taxes accrued would be siphoned off to this fund which would finance the functioning of Serbian media and Serbia television and that the Ustasha and the balija medias or, rather, the Sarajevo and the Zagreb media, and I mean television here, should be marginalised as much as possible." Now, this addition of the judge, that's new. You did not mention anything like that in your -- you didn't mention anything about a judge wanting to do these things when you gave evidence in the Brdjanin/Talic trial. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about the president of the court. You have it. You can check it in your documents. Well, if you think I'm not telling the truth, but of course I'm under an oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karabeg, the question is that where you testified in this Court about these remarks of a judge, whether you did not mention that judge or a judge when you testified in the Brdjanin and Talic case. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Your Honour, when I say chronology of events, I mean at one point I went back, but I had learned a lot in the meantime, ever since I returned in Sanski Most. I know much more now than I did at that point. I've taken also my notes, the notes that I had at home, and I refreshed my memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, no one is blaming you for anything at this moment, they're just about to establish what your testimony was in the Brdjanin and Talic case. So the question was, whether for good reasons or not is a different matter, the question is whether you mentioned this judge or a judge who spoke during this meeting when you testified in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't because I did not remember at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a clear answer. Ms. Loukas. Ms. Loukas might have some more questions because you'll not be surprised, and let me also once refer to you as being a lawyer, you'll not be surprised that Ms. Loukas and the Defence wonders why you didn't mention it at the time and why you do mention it now. That's an issue Ms. Loukas is interested in. So she'll put some questions to you. Try to answer these questions just as simple as possible. Listen to the question and give the answer to the best of your knowledge. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There's just a correction to the transcript. In response to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me for just a second, please. I'm not only a jurist, I'm also a lawyer, an attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't -- I think I said -- I think I said as being a lawyer, so I didn't mean to say anything else than a lawyer, which is a very general description. Ms. Loukas, you'd like to make a correction -- or to suggest that the transcript contains an error?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In response to a question from me. The response is at page 14, line 9: "I was talking about the president of the court. You have it. You can check it in your documents." I understand that that was apparently mistranslated, Your Honour, and part of the answer included "You can check it through your lines in Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it can be checked. I had some difficulties in finding it because my LiveNote had a late start this morning, so I've got it at a different place. But Mr. Karabeg, it is translated to us, one of your answers, as "I was talking about the president of court. You have it. You can check it in --" and it reads in our transcript "your documents." And the Defence asks our attention for the fact that you said not "you can check it in your documents" but you said a different thing in your own language. Could you repeat what you said in this respect. It was just prior to saying "If you think I'm not speaking" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few minutes ago? A couple of minutes ago, I said that I could check it through my connections. I wasn't referring to the Court but to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a bit confusing to me at this moment. Ms. Loukas, how important is it that it should be --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Clarified at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- clarified? Is it a vital part of the testimony or is it just some kind of an in between remark?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Not important at this particular time, I don't think, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I think we can move on. I take it the Prosecution concede there's nothing stated about ethnic cleansing or this particular judge in the Brdjanin/Talic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I agree that nothing was said about the particular judge. I would direct counsel and the Court's attention to page 6072, lines 12 through 18, which, although it does not specifically use the term "ethnic cleansing" we think it is something that could be interpreted as referring to that topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, but I am referring to the term "ethnic cleansing." So I think the Prosecution concedes the term "ethnic cleansing" doesn't appear and evidence about the judge doesn't appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I fully understand that whenever reference is made to any page which is the examination-in-chief, the Chamber does not have it in front of it, so we would like then to receive the specific pages, not the whole of it, so that we at least can understand what you said. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I'd like a Defence document to be placed before the witness. That's document "Agreement on the Formation of a Community of Bosnian Krajina Municipalities, dated 29th April 1991."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this a new document or an existing document?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's an existing document, in fact, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It has already been introduced as evidence. Prosecution Exhibit, page 65, binder 1, tab 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think it was introduced during Mr. Treanor's testimony, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You will understand that we didn't take all the 18 binders of Mr. Treanor with us. Ms. Thompson, I think the Treanor exhibits are --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can indicate that not only is it already a Prosecution exhibit, but we also included it in the Defence bundle, a copy of it. So it might be easier for the Registry assistants, in view of the fact that Ms. Philpott is not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's put it on the ELMO, if we have the right document, if the parties could. First have a look at the front page so that we are certain we're looking at the right document, and then we'll sort out which exhibit number exactly has been given to it. Front page on the ELMO, let me just see. Yes, is it clear what document we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So Mr. Karabeg, what you have before you is a Prosecution exhibit already in this case. It's an Agreement on the Formation of a Community of Bosnian Krajina Municipalities, dated the 29th of April 1991. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand you. Would you please so kind and repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Do we agree that what you have in front of you is a document "Agreement on the Formation of a Community of Bosnian Krajina Municipalities, dated 29th of April 1991"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: On paper, yes. Whether the document is legal or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So you're aware, are you not, that at the end of April 1991, these various municipalities combined to form this community of Bosnian Krajina municipalities? You're aware of that, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that was actually the topic of discussion, was it not, at that meeting you went to in March 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't actually remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just moving on to another topic and leaving that aside --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I formally tender that document, Your Honour. Well, I don't formally tender it, I mean it's already, but for the purposes of this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's recalled in respect of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving on to another topic, you know Adil Draganovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you're aware that there have been certain charges against Mr. Draganovic? Sorry, I didn't hear the response, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Draganovic has been accused of certain matters --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I need to interrupt at this point. I think he has answered he doesn't know. So I don't know what further discussion about that will gain us from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, do you want to assist the witness to verify whether he really doesn't know anything about it, or is it anything else? I will give you --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There are other matters, Your Honour, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A mere answer that someone doesn't know is not a point where everything should stop immediately, Mr. Hannis, so I'll give some room to Ms. Loukas to explore the matter further.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I may offer something at this point, Your Honour. If the purpose is to impeach Mr. Draganovic's testimony, which has come in under Rule 92 bis (D), if the Defence is willing to discuss with us what she wants to raise, we might be willing to stipulate to that and it's not necessary to raise it with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you just received an offer, I think. Is it something that would change your course of examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it will certainly streamline what I want from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the problem is that it first has to be discussed between the parties before you can finally make up your mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's part of the problem, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be of any assistance if I would allow -- I mean, I don't know how much time that would take, but would -- let's say a couple of minutes, would that assist you in making up your mind whether you should put the questions you had in mind to this witness or whether you could rather deal with the matter in other terms, the 92 bis (D)?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Prosecution and I can come to an agreement in relation to certain material that relates to a witness that's come in under 92 bis, there is a whole series of documents that we can perhaps agree that can be tendered, which would mean that I would only need to ask probably two-thirds the questions on this topic of this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you think it would take you to-- would it be of any use to give you a couple of minutes now so in order to?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think it might be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do it the following way: I'll give you -- we'll adjourn just for a couple of minutes, five minutes, and after this five minutes, I'd like to know whether there's any -- whether there's any result or if there's any expectation that a result could be achieved in a shorter time than it would take to --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I'm sure we can come to an agreement on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn for five minutes. That means that we would resume 2 minutes past 10.00. I have to ask your patience for short a period. --- Break taken at 9.56 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Strictly kept to the five minutes. Now, the next question is whether this results in an agreement between the parties on what is necessary to put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Fortunately, it does, Your Honour. Mr. Hannis and I have agreed that there's a bundle of Rule 68 material that has been -- that I have in relation to Mr. Adil Draganovic, which Mr. Hannis is happy to go to the Chamber in respect of this particular municipality and the fact that Adil Draganovic comes in under 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And this will only leave me I think two questions on the topic with this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. The Chamber is pleased by this efficient cooperation between the parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, you're aware, are you not, that on the 18th of March 2003, Judge Adil Draganovic was suspended? His appointment as a judge was suspended. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And are you aware that in his accused's response, his response as the accused for the introduction of evidence through witness testimony, he has cited -- he cited you as a potential witness?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So you're not aware that he has suggested what your evidence might be that might be able to assist him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we never discussed anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Did you discuss anything with his lawyers?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which lawyers you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Mr. Adil Draganovic's lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that he had any.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You don't know how this suggestion that you would give evidence for Mr. Draganovic emerged, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, what trial do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Karabeg, Mr. Draganovic has suggested in documents before the Bosnia-Herzegovina court that you would give evidence for him in relation to charges against him. That's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did testify, but he never said that I would testify or give evidence for him. Because I was the minister at that time when he was the president of the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. And -- well, prior to you giving evidence, you as a lawyer would know that often documents are presented in relation to the fact that you might give evidence.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a lawyer, and this is the 14th time you have mentioned me as being a jurist since yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the B/C/S/English interpretation --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I think perhaps when I say "lawyer" it's being interpreted as "jurist."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the interpreters would like to clarify the issue. I do not hear anything. But Mr. Karabeg, there seems to be a translation. Where we say "lawyer," that it's translated into your language in such a way that you respond to us that you're a lawyer. That's exactly what Ms. Loukas has said before and what I said before. So don't worry about that, that there's any misunderstanding as to your position as a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm not worried about that. But there's no need for her to mention that. So if I were a stonemason, she would say Mr. Karabeg, mason. So it doesn't need any qualification. She needn't use that word, because she is alluding to something when she says that. I'm conscious that I'm giving testimony under oath, under the solemn declaration here, so she needn't keep mentioning, and I've counted 15 times that she's mentioned the word.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The word is "pravnik" or "advokat," lawyer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm conscious of the capacity in which I'm giving testify here under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes an allusion is made to you as better understanding certain matters than, perhaps, a greengrocer would do. I think when it's limited to that, then it's just about your understanding. It has got nothing to do with the truthfulness -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that is precisely why she should not use the word in B/C/S "pravnik" because I'm an advokat, lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It just has been explained to us that there are two ways of translating what we say in English "lawyer," that's "pravnik" or "advokat." And it seems that you would prefer, if addressed as a lawyer, that it be translated by "advokat." Let's proceed and let's not spend too much time on this just to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, might I just be allowed to explain, Your Honours. I do not wish the Defence counsel to use either of those words. She need not refer to me by my profession. She can call me Witness Karabeg or Mr. Karabeg. There's no need for her to give an epithet like "lawyer."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes it's functional, and I'll allow Ms. Loukas under these circumstances to use that. If she would use it as to remind you that you would speak the truth and therefore would use this qualification, I would not allow her to do so. So if that's clear, we can proceed now. Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I think in the 21st century the use of the term "lawyer" has become a term of abuse.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the meaning of what the witness said. Could he please repeat if he wishes to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters could not translate what you just said, Mr. Karabeg. Would you please repeat your words or explain what you said, if it's of any relevance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not what I deserve and does not serve purpose or is not to my honour when she mentions for 15 times "you as a lawyer," "you as a lawyer." She need not do that. Because she says "you as a lawyer should know or ought to know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a clear answer to this objection. To what extent I would allow it, to what extent I would not allow it, and there's no further need for debate on this at this very moment. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, I will not refer again to the fact that you are a lawyer. I can promise you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Going on to another topic, I think, at this stage. Firstly, if the Defence Exhibit typewritten information sheet in English and B/C/S, that's number 3 and 4 on our list, could be placed before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I think you have that particular document before you, Mr. Karabeg? If you might just read through that document --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: -- in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: "According to verified --"

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, no, to yourself. You can read it out if you like. Why don't you read it out. Not a bad idea.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll read it to myself. Yes, I've finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, so you're aware, are you not, that as at the 7th of March 1992 it was considered that there were a number of people in the Sanski Most area in Green Beret uniforms with automatic rifles, and that an attack was sought to be launched on the Serbian village of Suhaca, and that it's considered that the people responsible for the SDA's activities Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in the local area in this regard include you. You're aware of that allegation, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: For what quotations? What allegations?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I pose a question at this point. I have seen this document. It's signed with the name or the reference "Milos." There are a number of documents in this case from this individual or this organisation. I'm not sure if the Court would like to inquire whether the defendant or the Defence is contending that those documents are legitimate and credible, because if so, we have a number of others that we would propose in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the document is legitimate is another question, but we find at this moment in front of us a text, and of course the original will look different, but could you give us any information about what it is, where it comes from. Unless the witness would know, then of course you can ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course, the source of this information is the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any further information as to where it comes from?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We do have some further information about that, but Your Honour, I would prefer not to discuss that in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps, the question to you, Mr. Karabeg, was whether you were aware that allegations are made, at least in this document, about an attack prepared by Green Berets, and your name is mentioned in this document as one of the mainly responsible persons of that. And the question was whether you were aware of this allegation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. And I would like to respond to this. This was a distorted presentation from Dzedovaca on the village of Kamengrad and the mosque. These were targeted with three shells, and the people gathered together and protested. So I think that anybody could write pieces of paper like this. Yes, I was present, but it was after --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just stop you, Mr. Karabeg. The first question, and I repeated the question put by Ms. Loukas, is whether you were aware of it. Your answer is no, I was not aware of this allegation. But from your subsequent answer, it appears that you have some knowledge of an event which you think is described in this piece of paper. If Ms. Loukas would like to have any further information about that, she'll ask you about it. Yes, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But please, Your Honour, may I be allowed to give an answer, to respond? I'm here as a witness to tell the truth and not to respond in the way she would like me to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you may have noticed, the Chamber keeps a close eye on the way you are examined by the parties. I'll first give an opportunity to Ms. Loukas to put any additional questions. If then finally you'd like to add something, I'll give you an opportunity. Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Karabeg, you've answered that you're not aware of this allegation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I read it from here, this is not correct. It's not. There's something there, but it's not correct in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. So what's correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is correct is that I was there. It is correct that it was in Kamengrad. It is correct that those three shells were shot from Dzedovaca onto Donji Dzedovaca and the mosque there and that the people had rallied to protest. And you don't mention that before that, three shells were targeting the mosque from the Serb villages. That is what is not mentioned. But yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you're saying that it's not true that you were in any way involved with this -- the Green Berets and arming of Muslims along with the other people mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, it is true, though, isn't it, that when you noticed that the -- in 1991 that the JNA were doing practices in the local area involving two teams, that you, when you and others learned about what was happening with these JNA practices in 1991, you tried to do something about it. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what. I'd like you to tell me what it was that I tried to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you called and had meetings with non-Serbs who had been serving with the JNA and had reserve ranks in the JNA, and now had different occupations to see what could be done to protect the Serbs -- the non-Serbs, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. It's not correct. It's fabricated, made up.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Where and when and with whom. I would have to hear where, when, and with whom.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, did you say anything like that to anyone from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Never. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, the next Defence Exhibit, Your Honour, if that could be shown to the witness, that's referred to in 1 and 2 on our list of documents. There's the English version and the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, just to identify what we have before you, this is the outline of an interview given by you on the 30th and 31st of May 1997. Now, do you agree with me that that's what this document represents?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You just land me with this all of a sudden, so I don't know. But yes, I think it is. Out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you'll notice that the document has headings. If you might turn to the heading marked "JNA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's page 3 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may pose a question at this point. This document was never signed nor initialled by this witness, so I'm not sure if we should inquire further before we go into details of what's in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is aware that it's not signed, and even contains parts which seems not to be an expression of what the witness said at that time, but gives some comments or even opinion about it. But the Chamber is aware of that. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, back on the 30th and 31st of May 1997, you were interviewed by Jutta Paczulla and Brenda Hollis from the Prosecution. That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You don't know if you were interviewed by Jutta Paczulla and Brenda Hollis on the 30th and 31st of May 1997?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't know. I gave so many statements in that respect, and now you're asking me something specifically relating to 1997, whether I remember that particular thing. And it was unfortunate that I was interviewed on the -- when it was the worst, 1995, 1996, and the 7th of May when I was under stress, because they were all the days when all this was happening to me, when I was arrested and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution concede that this is a record of an interview conducted on the 30th and 31st of May 1997 by Jutta Paczulla and Brenda Hollis from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have personal knowledge of that. I know that's what it says and that's what it appears to be, and we furnished it to the Defence because it related to this witness. However, I don't know whether it was ever read out to Mr. Karabeg or if he's ever adopted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not the question, whether it was read out or not. But whether this was a report of an interview by Jutta Paczulla and Brenda Hollis. May I ask you, Mr. Karabeg, do you remember that in May 1997 you were interviewed by two ladies from the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And there was also an interpreter present, Gordana Viskovic. Do you recall that, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, I take it what occurred there was that you spoke and various matters that might be included in your statement were written down. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And at the end, was the statement read out to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it was. But I don't know why I didn't sign it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But in any event, as you were speaking, notes were being taken of what you were saying. That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it ought to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, if you look at that heading under "JNA," I think that was pointed out to you by the court usher. You have that before you? You'll see that what I put to you is written down there, that 1991 there was a practice with the JNA. Practice with JNA. During these practices, exercises, there were two teams. They were -- the way the JNA practiced was how they later launched their attacks in this area. They did the practice in the area of Bosanska Krupa and Kljuc. When Karabeg and others learned about what was happening, they tried--

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So they called and had meetings with non-Serbs who had been serving with the JNA and who had reserve ranks in the JNA and now had different occupations to see what could be done to protect non-Serbs. So you see that what you've denied to me in court today is actually written down there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, this was after the colonel said that he spoken with the president of Krupa and that he had approved of those measures. And this is when I did this, after I realised that he had not -- that this was not going to work because we realised that everything from now on would be based on a one ethnic principle.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, the fact is, Mr. Karabeg, that you were very hesitant when you were giving this information to the Prosecution, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the answer. The interpreters could not hear you. The question was whether you were hesitant to give this information. Would you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You were hesitant, I think, Mr. Karabeg, because you had something to hide, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That's argumentative.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had nothing to hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I only have a short period to go, but I'm actually awaiting a document that will be faxed to the Defence room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's then adjourn until 11.00, and then the Judges will have time to consider whether they are planning additional questions to the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, just one matter relating to your statement where you listed the names of the people who were in the cell with you. And I don't know if you have the 1999 statement before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's paragraph 62.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Paragraph 62, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now they all appear to be Muslim names. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just very quickly through your statement, in relation to paragraph 35, you referred to having a list of names with you that they were very interested in. What was that list of names, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karabeg. Now, just one -- another matter, moving topics altogether, of course you were involved in the SDA and a politician. That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course you would have kept yourself well abreast of matters occurring at the head of the SDA, including in particular Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really. Yes, as far as the SDA generally speaking is concerned, but I did not have much contact with Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But were you aware that on a visit to Turkey in July 1991, at about the time when the war was nearly over in Slovenia and was about to begin in Croatia, Izetbegovic asked to join the Organisation of Islamic Countries?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was actually through the media that I learned about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you were aware, of course, that that move on the part of Mr. Izetbegovic antagonised Serbs and Croats?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that Bosnia and Herzegovina is still a member of that organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, but were you aware of the -- at that time that that caused some consternation amongst Serbs and Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I was a member of the local municipal SDA. I did not have any function at the level of BH as far as the SDA is concerned at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, Mr. Karabeg. But are you aware in your local area of that move perhaps causing some consternation amongst local Serbs and Croats?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, the question is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- simple, whether you are aware that it caused some consternation among the Serbs and the Croats that Mr. Izetbegovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I wasn't, because we didn't have any problems with Croats in Sanski Most, because in Sanski Most we were treated the same by the Serb community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, just for my information, if --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer to the question was no. No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, also in the evidence that you've given, you don't seem to indicate that anything happened to any of the Croats during this period you've given evidence to.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified about that. You are referring me now to the paragraph where I'm stating who I found when I got to the cell, and you have here the name and the surname of the Croat whom I found when I came to the cell.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. So in your entire evidence there is just this evidence in relation to one particular Croat who was in the cell with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th of May, I found those people there. They were not with me in the cell throughout that period. It was on the 25th of May, when I was detained, that I found them there.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'll leave that topic. Now, Mr. Karabeg, just --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If the witness might be shown a document. Unfortunately, this particular document just came through on the fax during the adjournment break. But I have copies for everyone in Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the Prosecution received a copy yet?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it's a relatively short document.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. It's in fact a photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to first give an opportunity to the Prosecution to have a glance at it before you put any question to the witness in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once the Prosecution has seen it, of course, the Chamber would very much like to have a copy as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I would indicate, Your Honour, that the document I've shown the Prosecution is, in fact, the one that was scanned, I think. In fact, yes, I think that's the actual scanned copy. The copies that I have for Court are photocopies of that scan, so they are obviously not as good as that particular one. In terms of exhibits, obviously that would be the particular exhibit. I just thought I'd point that out, and it's the one that should be shown to the witness because it has got a great deal more clarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll be happy to trade, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I should have taken my glasses, then, being the only one without.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, I almost gave away my copy as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, you have that document before you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course, the document is in B/C/S. You'll agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You'd agree with me a newspaper cutting from the 23rd of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can only assume. It is from Glas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Glas being a local newspaper at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Right. And you'll note the date is just under the headline there. You see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you see that this particular article refers to the gathering that you were speaking of in your evidence that you said you'd seen on TV?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is not it. This was on the news that day, the news programme, the daily news programme, with several footages, several stills, several photos.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You'll see that the photograph shows the front row of the gathering in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether this is the photograph. I didn't see this photograph on TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question seemed to assume that there was only one gathering in Banja Luka on that day, and I don't know that that is necessarily a fact. And Your Honour, because I don't have an English translation, I don't know what the headline is or what the description of this gathering is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we should first clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could ask -- could perhaps Ms. Cmeric read slowly the text. I wouldn't ask the witness to read something he -- could you perhaps slowly read the text, to start with, the heading.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "On the occasion of the 22nd of April, the day of liberation of Banja Luka, preparations for --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "On the occasion of the 22nd of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. April, the liberation day of Banja Luka, preparations for Defence. Troops and weapons are being brought to the banks of the River -- to the borders of Bosanska Krajina, and rivers of refugees are coming to these areas, Predrag Radic, president of the SO, stated yesterday at the session. Banja Luka, 22nd of April, this is the Remembrance Day, remembrance of all of those who gave their lives fighting for this country. However, it is also the day of preparations against those who are working against us. This was declared today at the ceremonial session of the Municipal Assembly on the occasion of the 22nd of April, the liberation day of Banja Luka. Before a full or a packed hall of the community centre of Banja Luka, the introductory speech was given by Mr. Predrag Radic, who greeted those who had gathered and emphasised that we're living in the times when dishonesty has come out of the dark and non-humans are walking around the area, and the Krajina region and Banja Luka as a town is being attacked by dogs of war from all over the world. "The borders of Bosanska Krajina have seen amassing of troops and weapons, and rivers of refugees are coming to this area which has become an island of peace. This was declared by Radic in his speech, who also expressed his good wishes to the combatants for peace and to all the guests. He wished them a lot of success in resisting these forces of evil so that this liberation day of Banja Luka could become -- would remain also an occasion to celebrate. "On this occasion, the guests were able to see a very rich cultural and arts programme. Signed by Z. Pejicic. Photographs by R. Ostojic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour. I believe there was one line beneath the photograph that wasn't read out. It's very small print on my copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that would be [Interpretation] "Ceremonial session at the community centre in Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At a certain moment, part of the translation was that it was a meeting or a gathering, perhaps, with guests, but of the Municipal Assembly. Is that a correct understanding, Ms. Cmeric, from what it says in the...?

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is actually the gathering that took place. That was a ceremonial session held in the Municipal Assembly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me --

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: -- and chaired by President Predrag Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check it. There seems to be a slight difference in what you tell us. Could you perhaps read it again in the original language so we can hear from the interpreters finally, because it was translated to us "This was declared today at the ceremonial session of the Municipal Assembly," which is not exactly the same as the ceremonial session in the Municipal Assembly. Could you perhaps read that part again slowly so that we can hear from the interpreters whether it was a ceremonial session of the Municipal Assembly or a ceremonial session in the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "This was declared at the ceremonial session of the Municipal Assembly today by the president, Mr. Predrag Radic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Ms. Loukas, please proceed. Now we at least know what the newspaper article tells us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, finally, are you prepared to concede that it's possible that you've made a mistake about Mr. Krajisnik being there on that date?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Loukas. Any need for questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one question I wanted to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know the Court does have a copy of the transcript of the direct examination of Mr. Karabeg in the Brdjanin case, but I want to read one question and one answer to him, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, I'm reading from page 6072 from Monday, the 27th of May, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley was cross-examining [sic] you, Mr. Karabeg. I want to read you the question and your answer and ask if you recall this. It regards that meeting in Banja Luka in early 1991. Question: "Now, you've said in your evidence that at the meeting what was put forward, the question was raised what to do with the balijas and Ustashas want. That was the jargon being used. Can you remember now after all these years anything specific that was said about the balijas and the Ustashas at this meeting?" Answer: "Well, they, it was said that the numbers of balijas and Ustashas should be reduced, that means should be assured for the Serbian Krajina, later the region, later the Republika Srpska, that their mini media of the balija and the Ustasha, this referred to Bosniak and Croatian televisions, and that all means should be used in order to prevent it from these media being seen and heard on this territory." Do you recall being asked that question and giving that answer in your testimony in the Brdjanin trial?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as you sit here today, do you recall that is what happened at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Canivell has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, you said yesterday that when you were asked, you and the Bosniak in your municipality, were asked to hand the weapons they may have, they complied because -- and you complied because you knew what could happen in case of a refusal. You didn't explain. What should have happened should have you refused to hand over these weapons, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would have killed us. And this is exactly what they did after. They would burn down the building. They would have probably surrounded it and destroyed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: How did you know about these results? You had had already some information about that happening in other places? Or how were you so sure about this result?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, before that, events had taken place already in Foca, in Brcko, and quite a few other places as well. The events in Sarajevo, for instance. And we were all able to follow this in the media, over the TV in particular. And especially later when we saw that from the direction of Dzedovaca or thereabouts, a column of 30 vehicles was moving, carrying armed soldiers of Serb ethnicity, members of the 6th Krajina Brigade, it was clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, I should like to clarify with your help several things. Mr. Fedad Karabeg, is he related to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? I didn't hear the name. What is the name of this person, Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fedad Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar. Well, if his surname is Karabeg, it is quite possible that we are related. But if he's, for instance, from Mostar, then we are not related at all. There is a street where -- in Mostar where the Karabeg family lives, but we are not related to them in any way. However, if he's from the area of Sanski Most, then it's quite possible that we are relatives or distant relatives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am now referring to what was written in Mr. Rasula's diary on the 25th of May 1992. Among other things, he says that Fedad, and I will quote you in English "owned a machine-gun, and his father a rifle." [Interpretation] That's why I asked you this question. I wanted to know if this particular individual is in any way related to you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Is he from Sanski Most? It is possible that he's a distant relative. But there are a lot of Karabegs. But I don't know this particular one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And my second question has to do with what you stated in your statement, the one that you gave in 1999. I'm referring to paragraph number 25 where you declare the following. I will quote your words in English: [In English] "In March 1992, I saw first time helicopters landing in Serb villages. I saw them go to Podlug, Dabar, et cetera, close to Sanski Most." [Interpretation] End of quotation. Later on, you said that you heard that those helicopters in fact were bringing in money to the villages, but that you doubted that information and that you insinuated, in fact, that those helicopters were bringing in weapons. Is that correct? Is that what you wanted to say, that the helicopters were, in fact, flying in munitions in order to arm the villages, the Serb villages? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because it was ridiculous for them to say that they were taking money to villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you never saw yourself any arms, any weapons in the helicopters themselves, yourself. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I wasn't even near those helicopters, nowhere near them, so I never saw that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I'd just like very briefly to refer to the meeting that you yourself spoke about that you attended in Banja Luka in March 1991. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
